h: Pleasure Gardens, Galleries and a Riverside Wander
p: Vauxhall has a long history of Londoners popping over the river for a bit of fun. From the 1600s to the mid-1800s, Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens was one of the city's great entertainment spots, with music, lantern-lit walks, fireworks and all sorts of fashionable goings-on. The site is now Spring Gardens, a park right by the farm, so you're stepping into a patch of the city that has been about fresh air and good times for centuries.

For a smooth visit, think about combining the farm with a picnic in the park next door, as it gives toddlers somewhere to run once they've said hello to the animals. If you've got a pony-mad child, look up the riding school's holiday activities well in advance, as places tend to go quickly. Charity farms like this rely on support, so the café and shop are good ways to chip in.

There's a lot within walking distance. Cross Vauxhall Bridge and you're at Tate Britain on Millbank, home to centuries of British art, with free entry to the main collection. Head along the Albert Embankment instead and you'll reach the Garden Museum at Lambeth, housed in a former church next to Lambeth Palace, with a lovely courtyard garden and café. Battersea Power Station, the iconic chimneyed landmark turned shops and restaurants, is a short hop west along the river, and you can ride the lift up one of its chimneys at Lift 109 for big views over London.
